channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Reports about mental health, supply issues aboard USS Lincoln raise concerns
item.description: The USS Lincoln has been at sea since late last year, part of the administration's war with Iran. Military families are worried about the conditions sailors are living under.
item.content:encoded: The USS Lincoln has been at sea since late last year, part of the administration's war with Iran. Military families are worried about the conditions sailors are living under.
item.dc:creator: Steve Walsh

item.title: Sen. Ruben Gallego on handling of USS Lincoln conditions: 'That's not proper leadership'
item.description: Lawmakers want answers from the Pentagon chief and the U.S. Navy about living conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona.
item.content:encoded:
Lawmakers want answers from the Pentagon chief and the U.S. Navy about living conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona.

(Image credit: AP)
item.dc:creator: Michel Martin

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard
item.description: A federal judge in Boston has dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit that claimed Harvard University did not do enough to protect students on campus from antisemitism.
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Boston has dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit that claimed Harvard University did not do enough to protect students on campus from antisemitism.
item.dc:creator: Jonaki Mehta

item.title: At Big Bend National Park, bulldozers begin clearing pristine desert land for border barrier work
item.description: A coalition of landowners, outdoor enthusiasts and business owners that say any work in Big Bend National Park would forever change the place often called "Texas' gift to the nation."

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: Lawmakers and families raise concerns about conditions aboard USS Lincoln, as the U.S.-Iran war drags on, Iranians seek a break from the conflict, Russian-held Crimea faces Ukrainian drone campaign.

item.title: Becky G on her new album and the importance of protecting spaces for Latino joy
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with multi-platinum singer, songwriter, and actress Becky G about her new album, "Baraja Bendita," which is Spanish for "blessed deck of cards."

item.title: Mike Huckabee says Israeli settlers attacking West Bank homes are 'terrorists'
item.description: Israeli settlers have besieged three homes in the occupied West Bank, including one owned by a Palestinian American. U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee referred to the settlers as "terrorists."

item.title: Record cyclosporiasis outbreak tests agencies hit by Trump administration's cuts
item.description: Last year's funding cuts to federal agencies that oversee foodborne illness outbreaks are being tested with the record cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S.

item.title: The money investors borrow to trade in the U.S. stock market is at an all-time high
item.description: Money that investors borrow to trade in the stock market is called margin debt. This debt is now above $1.5 trillion, 50% higher than a year ago. Could this spell trouble for the U.S. economy?

item.title: In Van, Turkey, Iranians seek a respite from the war between Tehran and the U.S.
item.description: The Iranian regime wants to drag out the war until the U.S. midterms. Meanwhile, many Iranians are voting with their feet.
